summary: Georgia Forestry Commission history says the first fire observation tower went up on the Ware Hotel in Waycross; the hotel is now an apartment community.

access.note: The building is now the Ware Hotel apartment community. No source describes public access to a tower on it.

events.note: The history says the first fire observation tower was erected on the Ware Hotel and links it, perhaps, to a 1928 forestry fair in Waycross. No source gives an erection date; 1928 is the fair's year.
Hotel Ware, the host building, opened on 21 February 1929 with 110 rooms.
A photo caption dates a restoration view of the hotel to 2011. The Florida Times-Union piece says W.H. Gross Construction was overseeing the reconstruction.

notes_for_editor: The Georgia Forestry Commission history places the first fire observation tower on the Ware Hotel after a 1928 Waycross forestry fair, hedged with the word perhaps; it gives no erection date. The hotel opened on 21 February 1929 (Vanishing Georgia; the Florida Times-Union piece says February 1929), so the tower's erection date falls on or after the fair and is not fixed by any source. The list's ware hotel entry (note first tower, 31.20980, -82.36091, 134 ft) is linked to the hotel by name and by the history's wording; the coordinates were not checked against the building footprint, and the hotel address per Fairway Management is 604 Elizabeth Street. No source describes the tower's removal, fate, or whether any part remains on the building. No staffing source found. The agency is not stated as a fact because the history does not name the tower's operator. The 2011 reconstruction is supported by a photo caption and the Florida Times-Union piece. The NRHP number NRIS 92000125 is from the UNF record.
